chapter: Later years and the Texas scene
title: What happened to Alphonso Trent and his band
summary: Trent died in Fort Smith; his band broke up in the early 1930s and no second Trent band existed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Oh, whatever happened to Trent now?
Trent died in his hometown, Fort Smith all this long.
But did he break his band up or were they going to decline or what?
Well, his band broke up in the early 30s. And one of his men just recently died in New York, Crook, the banjo player. And Leo Mosley is still jobbing in New York. He's doing a fantastic job.
What about a band like Trent? I've heard of Trent's number two band somewhere.
Oh, just some guy picked up Trent's name and used it. Trent never had a number two band. Yeah, well... As far as I can remember.

I know, the guys would get together and call themselves the young... Right, right. ...the Cedar Orchestra here, the young... It's just a branch. A branch. It's a branch. Right. And, but that wasn't a common thing there in Jackson.
No, no, it wasn't. Because you only had one Troy Floyd, you only had one Don Albert, and there was no substitutes or things like that.
